subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw own built-in pace-aware provider quota state and autonomous throttling, and what should the first supported scope be?
rationale: The remaining work defines provider-specific quota semantics, persistence, new config/defaults, status/tool prompt contracts, and autonomous blocking behavior that automation should not invent without maintainer product direction.

options.title: Visibility/context first
options.body: Expose pace context through provider usage, status, and session_status without automatic blocking, then revisit opt-in throttling after the data model proves useful.

options.title: Full core throttling policy
options.body: Design and implement an opt-in core policy that persists pace state and can throttle subagents or non-interactive work when configured thresholds are crossed.

options.title: Plugin/API primitives only
options.body: Keep core lean by adding missing generic provider usage or admission hooks while a plugin owns Anthropic-specific pacing policy.

recommendation.title: Visibility/context first
recommendation.body: Expose pace context through provider usage, status, and session_status without automatic blocking, then revisit opt-in throttling after the data model proves useful.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest adjacent current-main history for provider usage/status behavior and authored the most relevant merged implementation path.
